classification.difficultyReason: Compare raw scores, distances above the means and then calculated z-scores as additional information is supplied.

content.prompt: Tom scored 78% on a Science test and 72% on a Mathematics test.

children.label: a
children.prompt: In which test does Tom appear to have performed better?

answer.short: Science, based on the raw scores: 78% compared with 72%.
answer.worked: Looking only at the raw scores, Tom appears to have performed better in Science because $78\%>72\%$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The mean score for the Science test was 66% and the mean score for the Mathematics test was 62%. Using this information and Tom’s test scores, in which test does he appear to have performed better?

answer.short: Science: 12 percentage points above the mean, compared with 10 percentage points in Mathematics.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Science: }x-\mu&=78-66\\\text{Science: }x-\mu&=12\text{ percentage points}\\\text{Mathematics: }x-\mu&=72-62\\\text{Mathematics: }x-\mu&=10\text{ percentage points}\end{align*}$$
Based on the distances above the means, Tom still appears to have performed better in Science.

children.label: c
children.prompt: The standard deviation of the scores for the Science test was 6% and the standard deviation of the scores for the Mathematics test was 4%. Using all the information you now have, in which test has Tom performed better? Explain your answer.

answer.short: Mathematics: $z_M=2.5$, compared with $z_S=2$. His Mathematics result was further above its mean in standard deviation units.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}z_S&=\frac{x_S-\mu_S}{\sigma_S}\\z_S&=\frac{78-66}{6}\\z_S&=2\\z_M&=\frac{x_M-\mu_M}{\sigma_M}\\z_M&=\frac{72-62}{4}\\z_M&=2.5\end{align*}$$
Tom performed better in Mathematics relative to the group because its z-score is higher. His Mathematics score was 2.5 standard deviations above the mean, compared with 2 in Science. The smaller standard deviation in Mathematics means its scores were more tightly clustered around the mean.
